title: Partial-agreement lower bounds for EC discrete-log interpolation
question: Partial-agreement lower bounds (proof attempt). Let E/F_p, P of prime order r, N < min(p, r), A ⊆ {1..N} with |A| = m, and f a rational function on E regular at kP (k ∈ A) with f(kP) = k mod p for k ∈ A. (1) For every 1 <= j <= N-1: deg f >= T_j/2 where T_j = #{k : k, k+j ∈ A} (h_j = f∘τ_{jP} − f − j vanishes at those kP; h_j ≢ 0 since otherwise the pole set is jP-invariant, orbits of size r). (1b) Since Σ_j T_j = C(m,2): deg f >= m(m−1)/(4(N−1)) ≈ δ²N/4 for every δ = m/N. (1a) deg f >= ((2δ−1)N − 1)/2 for δ > 1/2. (1d) polynomial total degree >= deg f / 3. (2) x-only g with g(x(kP)) = k² on A: deg g >= S_j/3 with S_j = # 3-term progressions in A of difference j; gives deg g >= ((3δ−2)N − 2)/3 for δ > 2/3. N < p is necessary (counterexample p=5, r=7, f ≡ 1 on {1,6}).
rationale: From ECDLP-21; curve analogue of Coppersmith–Shparlinski-type approximation bounds.

next_action: Blind adversarial review; Lean formalization of (1b) is feasible by extending CurveX/Interpolation (pole-degree argument may be replaced by an x-only polynomial variant). Settle novelty vs Lange–Winterhof (theorem statements not yet accessed).
notes: PI checked the core counting (Σ_j T_j = C(m,2)) and the h_j ≢ 0 argument. Toy checks (p < 100) reproduced by PI: no violations; bound loose for sparse random A (true min ~ m polynomial, ~ (m+1)/2 rational), nearly sharp for intervals. Gap δ²N/4 vs (δN+1)/2 open. Only constrains low-degree algebraic formulas; no bit-complexity consequence.
